verdict.rationale: Braintrust's own docs say evals can 'Score outputs with LLMs, code, or humans', the SDK exposes a scorer factory based on trace assertions, and the API and MCP let users manage and author scorers. That establishes code-based scoring as a first-party capability, but the pack never shows an actual user-written custom scorer function: the GitHub example only plugs in the built-in LevenshteinScorer. Custom metrics and classifiers are mentioned, but how to define them is not documented here. missing for 10: an explicit worked example of a user-defined code scorer (function signature and return format), documentation of custom metric definition beyond a single mention, independent or hands-on corroboration of writing custom scorers.
